newsitem.title: USA: IMF to discuss quota increase, but no deal seen.
newsitem.headline: IMF to discuss quota increase, but no deal seen.

text.p: IMF members are due to review increasing quotas at talks here but are unlikely to reach agreement, Philippe Maystadt, head of the IMF's policy-making Interim Committee said on Saturday.
Quotas are contributions from member countries which provide the International Monetary Fund with its capital, which currently stands at 145.3 billion SDRs ($198 billion).
IMF managing director Michel Camdessus had been pressing for a doubling in quotas, though Maystadt said Camdessus had since come up with new proposals.
He declined to say what these were, but said in any case there were several issues to be sorted out before an accord was reached.
"I do not expect we could reach an agreement on this during the meeting," he told a news conference ahead of full ministerial meetings of the IMF and World Bank.
"I don't know if it will be possible to narrow the range (of differences on the size of the quota increase)," he said.
IMF members would have to agree not just on the size of the total increase in quotas, but also on its distribution across member countries.
One international monetary source said that member countries and the Fund were now discussing a 35 percent to 65 percent increase in quotas.

Among those countries insisting that the quota increase be at the low end of this 35 to 65 percent range were Britain, the United States and Canada, all reluctant to pump too much new money into the Fund, the source said.
Japan was arguing for an increase nearer to top end of this range.
The size of the quota contribution determines the number of votes a country has at the IMF.
